hosted.manageOnComputer: Manage it in Passwords on your computer.
hosted.notSetUp: Passwords is not set up on any of your computers yet: set it up in the Intentic desktop app, on the computer you want to keep them on.

lock.lockedNote: Names are shown while locked. Showing or copying a password asks you to unlock.

reset.lost: Forgot your passphrase and lost your recovery key?
reset.ask: Start Passwords over on this computer?
reset.saysEmpty: Passwords has nothing in it yet, so nothing is lost.
reset.says: The {count} password in it is set aside on this computer, not deleted, and opens again only with the old recovery key. | The {count} passwords in it are set aside on this computer, not deleted, and open again only with the old recovery key.
reset.then: This computer asks for an administrator's approval, then you turn Passwords on again with a new passphrase and recovery key.

list.label: Passwords
list.emptyAll: No passwords yet. They are saved here as you sign in.
list.recent: {count} saved this week while you signed in: {names} | {count} saved this week while you signed in: {names}
list.nothingSelected: Pick a password to see it here.

detail.worksNowhere: Not tied to a place yet.
detail.unverified: Not confirmed yet — it will be once it works.
detail.weak: This password is weak. Changing it on the site, then here, keeps the account safer.
detail.reused: This password is used for other accounts too.
detail.weakReused: This password is weak and used for other accounts too.
detail.backend: Read from {backend} each time it is used.
detail.noAgents: No sandbox is linked to this computer yet.
detail.deleteSays: Agents lose access to it, and it is gone from this computer. This can't be undone.

help.ask: Each use asks you on this computer first.
help.while-here: Used without asking while Passwords is unlocked on this computer.
help.always: Always keeps a copy in that sandbox, so it works when this computer is off.
help.off: This sandbox's agents cannot use it.

edit.title: Title
edit.addPlace: Add a site, app or ssh target
edit.anyFieldHelp: Not only password fields: for a code or a key a program asks for in a plain field.
edit.newDescription: Most passwords are saved as you sign in. Add one by hand when that is not possible.
edit.needTitle: Give it a title or a place it works.
edit.badPlace: “{place}” is not a site, app or ssh target.

requests.title: Requests
requests.empty: No agent is waiting for a password.
requests.wants: {sandbox}'s agent wants to sign in to {place}
requests.wantsAs: {sandbox}'s agent wants to sign in to {place} as {username}
requests.noMatch: No saved password fits. Type it once and it is saved here for next time.

settings.title: Settings
settings.rememberHelp: Passwords you type are saved here without asking. Agents get none of them until you say so.

sourceHelp.terminal: ssh, sudo and git prompts on this computer.
sourceHelp.apps: Password fields in programs: you type once into a small box of ours.
sourceHelp.sandbox: Hidden prompts in a sandbox terminal you type into.

settings.hello: Unlocking asks Windows Hello: your face, fingerprint or PIN.
settings.polkit: Unlocking asks for your computer's password.
settings.recoveryHelp: Your backup for emergencies: it opens your passwords if you forget your passphrase, Windows Hello is reset, or this computer is replaced. It was shown once, when Passwords was turned on.
settings.neverSaveEmpty: Nothing. A notice's “Never for this site” adds a place here.
settings.importHelp: A CSV file exported from Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox, Safari, 1Password, Bitwarden or KeePassXC.
settings.helloOff: Windows Hello is off for Passwords
settings.helloOffHelp: It was set up without it, so Passwords asks you to type your passphrase instead.
settings.unlockPassphrase: Unlocking asks for your passphrase. Your recovery key is the backup.
settings.unlockRecovery: Unlocking asks for your recovery key because no passphrase is set. Set one so the recovery key stays a backup.
settings.passphraseOn: Typed to unlock when Windows Hello or your computer's own check can't answer.
settings.passphraseOff: Not set, so Passwords asks for your recovery key instead. Set a passphrase and keep the recovery key as the backup.
settings.passphraseHelp: Passwords asks you to confirm on this computer first. Your recovery key stays as it is.

import.unknown: This file is not an export Passwords knows. Export a CSV from your browser or password manager and try again.
import.skipped: {count} row left out: no password, or no site it is used on. | {count} rows left out: no password, or no site they are used on.
import.deleteFile: The file still holds your passwords in plain text. Delete it once you are done.

first.hero: Your passwords stay on this computer. Agents use them without ever seeing them.
first.permission: Windows will ask once for permission to keep them where no program — agents included — can read them.
first.permissionLinux: Your computer will ask once for permission to keep them where no program — agents included — can read them.
first.recoveryHelp: If you forget your passphrase, Windows Hello is reset or this computer is replaced, this key opens your passwords. It is shown only now.
first.recoveryHelpNoHello: If you forget your passphrase, this computer's sign-in is reset or the computer is replaced, this key opens your passwords. It is shown only now.
first.fileSaved: Saved to your Downloads folder as {file}.
first.existingTitle: Passwords is already on this computer
first.existingHelp: It was set up before, so the passphrase you just chose was not kept and there is no new recovery key: what opened it before still does. Set or change the passphrase in Settings. If you have neither, choose “Forgot your passphrase and lost your recovery key?” beside the lock.
first.rememberTitle: Let Intentic remember the passwords you type
first.rememberHelp: Saved quietly as you sign in, with a notice you can undo. Agents get none of them until you say so.
first.importHelp: Import a CSV export from your browser or password manager, or skip this and let them be saved as you sign in.
first.helloSkipped: Windows Hello wasn't set up, so Passwords will ask for your passphrase until you turn Hello on in Settings.
first.passphraseHelp: You type it to unlock Passwords when Windows Hello can't answer. Next you get a recovery key, the backup for the day you forget it.
first.passphraseHelpNoHello: You type it to unlock Passwords when your computer's own check can't answer. Next you get a recovery key, the backup for the day you forget it.

unavailable.title: Passwords isn't available
unavailable.takesAWhile: This takes a minute or two. Keep this window open.

remember.strip: Let Intentic remember the passwords you type?

hello.strip: Windows Hello isn't turned on for Passwords, so it asks you to type your passphrase instead. Turn it on to confirm with your face, fingerprint or PIN.

removed.title: Recently deleted
removed.help: Deleted passwords stay here for 30 days. Put one back and it returns as it was, with the agents that could use it.
removed.none: Nothing was deleted in the last 30 days.
removed.cannotUndo: This can't be undone. Passwords asks you to confirm on this computer.
